title: Shrink width: depth 10, dim 512 (+ HEAD_DIM 64)
description: ASPECT_RATIO 64->51 (n_embd 640->512, 8 heads) and HEAD_DIM 128->64 at DEPTH 10; 60.8M params, 0.69x FLOPs/token, 377M tokens in 1439 steps.
reflection: NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.994916 vs 0.988076 baseline, +0.0068 (~14 sigma on the pooled 4.8e-4 floor). My arm contains HEAD_DIM 64, so the width shrink alone cost roughly +0.011. The down-side of the aspect axis is now sampled and it loses: the size box is closed on all four sides (deeper, shallower, wider, narrower all worse than 10 layers x dim 640). The curve is asymmetric though - shrinking costs ~0.011, the equivalent widening step cost ~0.030, so the minimum sits at or just below 64 and the penalty for erring small is 3x cheaper. Two things I got wrong and one I got right: (1) my engineering predictions were near-exact (61M params predicted / 60.8M actual, 2.97e8 FLOPs / 2.957e8, ~1500 steps / 1439), so the model was built as designed and the idea simply does not pay; (2) the token gain underdelivered - 0.69x FLOPs bought only 1.29x tokens, not 1.45x, because MFU fell 41.9% -> 37.3% on the smaller matmuls, so shrinking is penalised twice; (3) the 'tokens per parameter is binding' story is dead for good - this run went from 3.4 to 6.2 tok/param, the direction that story wanted, and lost. The most valuable by-product is an accidental matched pair: a2's round-0 arm was d8/dim512/HD64/batch 2^18 = 0.993500 and mine is d10/dim512/HD64/batch 2^18 = 0.994916, identical in every other respect. Depth 8 -> 10 at FIXED width is +0.0014, i.e. neutral-to-negative. So the cell's only large win (a5 round 0, -0.0093) was the WIDTH move 512 -> 640, not the depth move, and we have been calling it 'the depth win' for two rounds. Live follow-up that falls straight out of this: DEPTH 8 with ASPECT_RATIO 80 (dim 640, HD64) keeps the winning width at 0.8x FLOPs.
